Then $F\in C_c^\infty$ and $g_{t,f}(r,x)=\int\phi_{t-r}(w-z)F(w)dw$. Differentiation of the Gaussian convolution, followed by two integrations by parts against $F$, gives $\partial_rg_{t,f}=-L_rg_{t,f}$ and $|L_rg_{t,f}|\le\tfrac12\|F''\|_\infty$; the chain rule gives $L_rg=\tfrac12\partial_{zz}(g\circ h)$. The densities and all weighted coefficients $p b$, $p a$, and $\partial_x(pa)$ are jointly bounded on compact subsets of $[\epsilon,T]\times\mathbb R$, so the displayed local weighted integrals are finite; the spatial adjoint identity follows by compact-support integration by parts.
